packages.label: הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ וְשִׂמְחַת כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת
packages.label_en: The Root and the Joy of All Goods
packages.reason: These nodes all share the same essential nature: they are different facets of the spiritual principle that at the ROOT all goods are unified, and true joy consists in perceiving that unity. The Root (שרש) IS the state where all goods are one (כל הטובות ביחד); looking upward (הסתכלות למעלה) IS the Root (the text says 'דהיינו על השרש'); joy from all goods together (שמחה מכל הטובות ביחד) IS perfect/complete joy (שלמות וגדלות השמחה); and Jethro (יתרו) is the exemplar of this state — 'וַיִּחַדְּ יִתְרוֹ עַל כָּל הַטּוֹבָה' proves he was one who looked upward at the root. All are expressions of the same spiritual reality: the vantage point of the divine root from which all goods flow as one.

merge_notes.reason: The text equates these directly: 'שְׁלֵמוּת וְגַדְלוּת הַשִּׂמְחָה הִוא, מִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִשְׂמֹחַ מִכָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת בְּיַחַד.' Perfect joy IS joy from all goods together — two names for the same state, not a cause-effect sequence.

Jethro is the embodied example of the principle: 'וַיִּחַדְּ יִתְרוֹ עַל כָּל הַטּוֹבָה... כִּי הָיָה מִסְתַּכֵּל לְמַעְלָה עַל כָּל הַטּוֹבָה, הַיְנוּ עַל הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ.' Jethro IS the one who looks upward. He is not the cause of that looking, nor the effect — he is the person-dimension of the same essential reality.

packages.label: הַכְּלָלִיּוּת וְהַהִתְנוֹצְצוּת
packages.reason: These nodes share the essential nature of the mechanism by which unified joy produces amplified light. Inclusion (כלליות) IS the state of joy being included within its fellow (שמחה בחברתה) — the text defines them as identical. The sparkling (התנוצצות) from joy to joy IS the increase of light (נגדל ונתוסף האור) — they are two descriptions of the same phenomenon: what inclusion looks like in its active, luminous dimension. The multiplication of joys included together (ריבוי שמחות שנכללין ביחד) is the structural expression of this same reality. All these nodes articulate the same essential truth: when goods/joys are unified at their root, they illuminate each other and the light multiplies.

merge_notes.reason: The text defines them as identical: 'עַל־יְדֵי הַכְּלָלִיּוּת שֶׁנִּכְלָל שִׂמְחָה בַּחֲבֶרְתָּהּ' — inclusiveness IS joy being included within its fellow joy. One is the abstract principle (כלליות), the other is its concrete instantiation (שמחה בחברתה); they are parallel expressions of the same essential reality.

Sparkling (התנוצצות) and the light of joy (אור השמחה) are the two faces of the same luminous reality: 'נִגְדָּל וְנִתּוֹסֵף הָאוֹר מְאֹד, עַל־יְדֵי הִתְנוֹצְצוּת שֶׁמִּתְנוֹצֵץ מִשִּׂמְחָה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ.' The sparkling IS the light increasing. These are not cause-effect; sparkling is the name for the light's mode of amplification, and the amplified light is the name for what sparkling produces — at the level of essential nature, they are the same reality described from two angles.

packages.label: פִּירוּד הַשְּׂמָחוֹת — חִלּוּקִים
packages.reason: These nodes share the essential nature of spiritual fragmentation — the state in which a person's experience of good is divided rather than unified. Divisions (חלוקים) IS fragmentation (פירוד), which in this Torah functions as the evil/deficient counterforce to the unified joy of Package 1. Jealousy (קנאה) and anguish (צער) are the consequence that emerges when a person has no joy at all — even becoming resentful over a match-making (מקנא על השידוך). This is the anti-Jethro, the person stuck in the fragment who cannot rise to the root. The fragmented state is the evil mirror of the unified state of Package 1: where Package 1 shows all goods as one at the root, Package 3 shows the person trapped in the multiplicity who cannot access the root.

merge_notes.reason: Divisions (חלוקים) and fragmentation of joys (פירוד השמחות) are the same essential reality from two angles. The text opens: 'כִּי יֵשׁ חִלּוּקִים רַבִּים בְּעִנְיַן הַשִּׂמְחָה' — the many divisions ARE the fragmented state. One is the structural description (many divisions), the other is the experiential result (joys fragmented). They share essential nature: the absence of unity.

Jealousy and anguish (קנאה וצער) represent the furthest extreme of the fragmented state — not merely unable to rejoice from all goods, but unable to rejoice at all, and actively suffering from envy. They belong in the same evil package as חלוקים because they are the natural fruit of the divided state: 'יֵשׁ לוֹ קִנְאָה וָצַעַר, שֶׁמְּקַנֵּא עַל הַשִּׁדּוּךְ.' This is still the essential nature of division/separation, not a new domain.
